variants.task: Create /tmp/eval_bs/bs.py — Read from stdin: line 1 is the number of cases C (1 <= C <= 1000). Each next line is 'S K T r sigma' (5 floats: spot, strike, time-to-expiry in years, risk-free rate, volatility; S, K, T, sigma > 0 and r >= 0). For each line output, on its own line, the Black-Scholes European call price c = S*N(d1) - K*exp(-r*T)*N(d2) where d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r + sigma^2/2)*T) / (sigma*sqrt(T)), d2 = d1 - sigma*sqrt(T), and N(.) is the standard normal CDF. Format to 4 decimals. If your stdlib lacks erf, use the Abramowitz & Stegun 7.1.26 approximation (p=0.3275911, a1=0.254829592, a2=-0.284496736, a3=1.421413741, a4=-1.453152027, a5=1.061405429). Grading runs hidden cases in this format with an absolute tolerance of 1e-3 per price; /tmp/eval_bs/sample_input.txt and /tmp/eval_bs/sample_output.txt are a worked sample. Pure Python (standard library only).
